title: WATCH: Leanne Morgan's Daughter Dated Morgan Wallen… Then Ran - NewsBreak
text:
By Donny Meacham ,
2 hours ago
Before he was topping charts, growing the most famous mullet in music, and selling out stadiums, Morgan Wallen was just a sweet Southern guy… going on a few dates with comedian Leanne Morgan ’s daughter.
Yep. You read that right.
Leanne shared the hilarious (and surprisingly wholesome) story on a recent episode of Theo Von’s This Past Weekend podcast, and it’s as small-town sweet as you’d hope.
From Charity Gigs to Casserole Promises Wallen and Leanne first crossed paths years ago at a charity event in Knoxville, Tennessee — back when he’d just been cut from The Voice and was still working as a landscaper.
“That little thing was mowing, had mowing equipment, and we both got asked to do a charity thing,” Leanne recalled. “I think they paid us $200 — if they paid us anything.”
Read More: This Girl Landed a Gig With Morgan Wallen From a Home Video [Watch]
Morgan sang. Leanne did comedy. And backstage? She was immediately charmed.
Subscribe to Taste of Country on Youtube
“I thought he was so sweet and darling… I promised him a casserole,” she said. “He goes, ‘ I’m gonna try to make it in country music. ’ And I thought, ‘How is that little thing gonna go?’”
Turns out, that “little thing” went pretty far.
Morgan + Maggie? Some time after the event, Wallen took Leanne’s daughter, Maggie, on a couple of dates.
But a ccording to Leanne , it didn’t last — not because he wasn’t nice, but because Maggie quickly realized… “I think he likes wild girls that like to key cars.”
Read More: Morgan Wallen’s 2026 Still the Problem Tour Will Feature This Exciting New Stage Design [Pictures]
“See, my children went to a Christian school and were told not to,” Leanne joked. “She thought he was darling… but he liked girls that like to fight in the yard. And that’s okay! There’s pretty girls in Powell!”
Wallen may have been sweet, but Maggie was “cut from a different cloth.”
“We’re not fighters,” Leanne said proudly. “We’re lovers.”
A Near-Miss (and a Perfect Story) Did Maggie miss her chance at becoming the First Lady of Mullet Nation? Or did she dodge a very twangy tornado?
Either way, we’re obsessed with this story: a perfect Southern almost-love tale complete with charity gigs, casseroles, and one hilarious mama trying to make sense of it all.
And to be fair, if you’re gonna date a country star, at least make sure your mom’s a stand-up legend who’ll tell the story later.
30 Best Morgan Wallen Songs Every Fan Should Know by Heart You'll find largely singles in this Top 30 countdown of Morgan Wallen 's best songs and biggest hits. But we've scattered in a few songs found deep within Wallen's three albums, If I Know Me and his record-breaking double albums Dangerous and One Thing At a Time .
We've even included a few early favorites from his 2025 project, I'm the Problem . Amy Sussman, Getty Images for MRC No. 30: "Your Bartender" Tapping into heartbreak, "Your Bartender" is a plea to get back the love of Wallen's life. Realizing that begging probably won't work, he wishes he could take on the role of someone or something this mystery girl will listen to — like a bartender, her car, the Bible, anything.
Wallen wrote the song with fellow artists Thomas Rhett and Rhett Akins, among others. It appears on his Dangerous: The Double Album , which arrived in 2021. Nicholas Hunt, Getty Images No. 29: "Whiskey'd My Way" Another Thomas Rhett co-write, "Whiskey'd My Way" was a part of Dangerous: The Double Album . In this heartbroken track, Wallen finds himself turning to whiskey to get over an ex. While others would call their mama or read a self-help book, Wallen leans on brown liquor to see him through. Rick Diamond, Getty Images for Country Thunder No. 28: "Talkin' Tennessee" Wallen takes on the role of Southern gentleman in "Talkin' Tennessee." After meeting a girl who is sick of the city fellas, Wallen hopes to show her what a country boy can do. He (respectfully) lays it out for her, sharing in detail how their love story will unfold.
"Talkin' Tennessee" is the final track on his 2018 album If I Know Me . Jason Kempin, Getty Images for Country Music H No. 27: "Me on Whiskey" With a strong affinity for whiskey, Wallen included "Me on Whiskey" on the second disc of Dangerous: The Double Album . Although he did not write the song, it falls in line with much of the project. Rodney Clawson, Mark Holman, and Ernest K. Smith (known as Ernest) wrote this song.
The cheeky love song finds Wallen and his flame "gettin' Tennessee tipsy in the neon light ." What starts as an innocent date night turns steamy after Wallen gets into the whiskey and she gets into the wine. Rich Fury, Getty Images for iHeartMedia No. 26: "Silverado for Sale" Wallen finds himself trading in his most prized possession for something better: By selling his Silverado, he can finally purchase that diamond ring and get down on one knee. In the ad he's crafting for its sale, he boasts about how that truck got him the girl — a means to an end, if you will.
Written by Dallas Davidson, Marv Green and Ben Hayslip, "Silverado for Sale" is found on disc two of Dangerous: The Double Album . Big Loud No. 25: "Cover Me Up" While on tour with Luke Combs, Wallen's cover of Jason Isbell's song became a staple onstage. The song is deeply personal for Isbell, as he wrote it about his wife Amanda Shires after his battle with alcoholism.
Wallen released "Cover Me Up" as a promotional single prior to releasing Dangerous: The Double Album. It charted on both the Billboard Hot 100 and the Hot Country Songs chart. His version of the track was certified 4X Platinum by the RIAA, selling more than 4,000,000 copies in the US. Kevin Winter, Getty Images for iHeartRadio No: 24: "Still Goin' Down" Wallen teamed up with his buddy Hardy to write "Still Goin' Down" alongside Ryan Vojtesak. The track was released as a promotional single leading to the release of his double album, Dangerous .
The song is an anthem for small-town Friday nights. Wallen sings of gathering with friends in an open field and sipping beer underneath the stars around a big bonfire. The track charted on both the Billboard Hot 100 and the Hot Country Songs charts and was certified Platinum after selling more than 1,000,000 copies. Erika Goldring, Getty Images for ACM No. 23: "Somebody's Problem" Wallen released several songs to help promotes his double album, Dangerous . Although they weren't official radio singles, they still performed well. "Somebody's Problem" was certified 2X Platinum after selling more than 2,000,000 copies and charted on both the Billboard Hot 100 and the Hot Country Songs charts.
Ernest, Jacob Durrett and Rodney Clawson were all co-writers with Wallen on "Somebody's Problem." In the song, Wallen finds new love and wonders how the last guy ever let this woman go. He assumes she must have been somebody's problem and happily accepts that she is about to be his problem next. Big Loud No. 22: "The Way I Talk" "The Way I Talk" served as the lead single off Wallen's debut studio album, If I Know Me . The song was written by Jessi Alexander, Ben Hayslip and Chase McGill and arrived Sept. 12, 2016, essentially launching Wallen's career.
Wallen said the song was a perfect fit for him, as it touched on the way he lives his life and the things he is proud of. "The Way I Talk" taps into his Southern roots and presents them unapologetically. The track charted on the Billboard Hot Country Songs chart and became his first single to find its way onto the Country Airplay chart. Big Loud/Apple Music No. 21: "Don't Think Jesus" “Don’t Think Jesus” is a deviation from Wallen’s typical country songs, but it’s not out of character for the self-proclaimed Christian. The song finds Wallen singing about falling short of people’s expectations and disappointing those he loves. He admits his faults, believing God must be disappointed in him, and yet, he believes that Jesus extends grace to those who don’t deserve it.
Wallen didn’t release this one as a single that was buttoned up and ready to go to country radio. Instead, he shared the song on social media in Oct. 2021, playing the song on his guitar. The track was not written by Wallen, but he liked it enough to include it on his album One Thing at a Time . Big Loud No. 20: "Up Down" ft. Florida Georgia Line While "Up Down" may not have been Wallen's debut single, it certainly catapulted him into the world of mainstream country music. Written by Hardy, Brad Clawson and CJ Solar, Wallen recruited Florida Georgia Line to join him on the track. He said the song resonated with him because it reminded him of having a good time in his small hometown.
"Up Down" reached No. 1 on the Billboard Country Airplay chart and No. 5 on the Hot Country Songs chart. It was certified 4X Platinum by the RIAA for selling more than 4,000,000 copies. Big Loud No. 19: "7 Summers" Written by Wallen, Josh Osborne and Shane McAnally, "7 Summers" was originally left off the tracklist for Dangerous: The Double Album . However, a demo version of the song on social media gained so much popularity among fans, he decided to include it. Eventually it would become the second single off the project, arriving Aug. 14, 2020.
"7 Summers" broke the single-day streaming record for a country song on Apple Music. It also debuted at No. 1 on Billboard 's Hot Country Songs charts and even peaked at No. 6 on the all-genre Hot 100 chart. Wallen became the second male country artist to debut a song in the Top 10 on the Hot 100. The RIAA certified the track 3X Platinum after it sold more than 3,000,000 copies. Big Loud No. 18: "Sand in My Boots" Wallen has proven he can bring the party with his uptempo anthemic tracks, but he can just as easily slow things down for a ballad. "Sand in My Boots" is a nostalgic, heart-tugging song that reminisces on a love that could have been. Hardy wrote the track alongside Josh Osborne and Ashley Gorley.
The song served as Wallen's third single from his record-breaking Dangerous: The Double Album . "Sand in My Boots" became his fifth No. 1 hit on the Billboard Country Airplay chart and was certified 2X Platinum with more than 2,000,000 copies sold. No. 17: "Smile" Wallen finds himself reminiscing about an old relationship in “Smile.” Long after their love has gone cold, he stares longingly at a photo of them out with friends. She has a big smile on her face. He can’t help but think about how nice it is to see her so happy, even if it was just for the picture, and even if it was before things went sour.
“Smile” was first shared on social media by Wallen without much context in Aug. 2024. He then surprise released the song on New Year’s Eve along with a music video. The song climbed into the Top 5 on both the Billboard Hot 100 and Hot Country Songs charts. Big Loud No. 16: "More Than My Hometown" Anyone who grew up in a small town knows there are some people who will never leave it. In "More Than My Hometown," Wallen is one of them. Despite caring from someone very deeply, he draws the line at moving away from the place that brought them together.
Wallen wrote the track with Hardy, Ernest and Ryan Vojtesak. The song served as the lead single from Dangerous: The Double Album . It was certified 4X Platinum. "More Than My Hometown" reached No. 1 on the Billboard Country Airplay chart. Terry Wyatt, Getty Images No. 15: "I Ain't Comin' Back" ft. Post Malone It’s clear Wallen isn’t interested in rekindling a romance with this former lover in “I Ain’t Comin’ Back.” Following an argument with his ex, he has made up his mind, and he’s gone like Richard Petty.
The track is the second collaboration between Wallen and Post Malone. The pair also crafted “I Had Some Help” which Malone selected for his 2024 country album F-1 Trillion . Wallen wasn’t about to let this one get left in the dust, so he picked it up for his album I’m the Problem . Big Loud No. 14: "Whiskey Glasses" While "Whiskey Glasses" was a part of Wallen's EP The Way I Talk , it was also released as the third single off his debut studio album, If I Know Me . The song was written by Ben Burgess and Kevin Kadish and topped both the Billboard Country Airplay and Hot Country Songs charts. It has also been certified 7X Platinum by the RIAA, selling more than 7,000,000 copies.
"Whiskey Glasses" takes inspiration from the idea of rose-colored glasses. Rather than seeing things for what they are, Wallen opts for whiskey glasses to prevent him from seeing the truth. When you're feeling poor, just pour yourself another drink is his motto. Big Loud No. 13: "Chasin' You" "Chasin' You" was penned by Wallen with Jamie Moore and Craig Wiseman. The song became his third consecutive chart-topper, reaching No. 1 on the Billboard Country Airplay chart. It has since been certified 4X Platinum.
The song finds Wallen heartbroken after losing the love of his life. No matter what — or who — comes his way, he'll always be chasing that first love, he sings. He released an artistic visual to accompany the song: It's a black-and-white video that features Wallen driving around town in a convertible. Big Loud No. 12: "Wasted on You" "Wasted on You" takes inventory of everything that's been wasted on an ex. In addition to the time and money, Wallen says he's said sorry way too many times for things he didn't do. He wrote the song with Ernest, Josh Thompson and Ryan Vojtesak.
Released as the fourth and final single from Dangerous: The Double Album , "Wasted on You" debuted at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot Country Songs chart. The song found itself in the Top 10 alongside Wallen's songs "Somebody's Problem," "Warning," "Sand in My Boots," "7 Summers" and "More Than My Hometown." He's the first artist to ever place six songs in the Top 10 on that chart at the same time.
Wallen also became the first artist to simultaneously top both the Hot Country Songs and the Top Country Albums charts, as Dangerous was No. 1 on the latter. "Wasted on You" has been certified 3X Platinum with more than 3,000,000 copies sold. Mike Coppola, Getty Images No. 11: "Just in Case" Wallen is hung up on an old flame in “Just in Case.” Even though his heartbreak doesn’t keep him at home alone, he keeps his heart extremely guarded. Sure, he’s dated others and done his best to move on, but he never allows himself to fall in love, just in case his old lover comes back around.
“Just in Case” was released ahead of I’m the Problem, his fourth studio album and quickly started climbing the Billboard Hot Country Songs chart. The song is quite catchy for a ballad and has caught the attention of his fans who also have a “Just in Case” ex-lover. Big Loud/Apple Music No. 10: "Love Somebody" Wallen pines for real love in “Love Somebody.” He’s tired of the brief trysts and the women who are just looking for a piece of the spotlight. Instead, he wants the putting down roots kind of love that lasts forever.
"Love Somebody" was the second single off Wallen’s I’m the Problem . After its release in Oct. 2024, the song quickly became a No. 1 hit. It reached the top of the Billboard Country Airplay, Hot Country Songs and Hot 100 charts. The track has also become popular overseas, reaching Top 10 status in several countries, like the Netherlands, Norway and Sweden. Big Loud/Apple Music No. 9: "I'm the Problem" “I’m the Problem” turns the breakup blame game on its head. Wallen isn’t afraid to admit his faults in the failed relationship, but he doesn’t believe he was the root of all the problems, either. In the chorus, he sings, “ If I’m the problem, you might be the reason ” as he points the finger back at the match that ignited the flame.
The song is the title track for Wallen’s fourth studio album. He initially shared the song under the name “I Guess” before rebranding it as “I’m the Problem.” Since its release on Jan. 31, 2025, it has reached the peak position on both the Billboard Country Airplay and Hot Country Songs charts. Erika Goldring, Getty Images No. 8: "Superman" “Superman” is by far Wallen’s most personal song yet, because it’s all about his son, Indigo.
The lyrics find him in a vulnerable spot talking about his past mistakes and the fact that one day his son will read about them online. It pains him to think that the little boy who believes he is Superman will one day discover that he’s not.
After several attempts to write something for his son, wanting it to be just perfect, the country singer shared the track on social media. It was later revealed that the song would be a part of his album I’m the Problem . Wallen opted to put the song out just one week prior to the album’s release, giving it its own special moment in the spotlight. Amy Sussman, Getty Images No. 7: "Thinkin' Bout Me" In "Thinkin’ Bout Me," Wallen finds solace in his heartbreak knowing his ex-flame won’t be able to get him out of her mind. Even though she’s moved on — which can be hard to watch for a scorned lover — he knows she’s gonna be thinking about him. He even taunts her in the chorus, singing, “When you’re tastin’ what he’s drinkin’, are you thinkin’ ‘about me?”
Wallen dropped the track in Sept. 2023 as the sixth single off his One Thing at a Time album. The song was pushed to country radio and became a No. 1 single on the Billboard Country Airplay chart, while reaching the third position on the Hot Country Songs chart. Big Loud/Apple Music No. 6: "Lies Lies Lies" Even though the flame has gone out, Wallen is still holding onto hope that the romance can be revived. Oh, he’ll claim he doesn’t think about her and it doesn’t hurt to see her with someone else, but those are all lies. And while he admits his lies, he hopes she will tell some lies of her own and tell him that she wants him back.
Released in July 2024, “Lies Lies Lies” served as the lead single off Wallen’s I’m the Problem album. The song reached the peak of the Billboard Country Airplay chart and even worked its way up to No. 15 on the publication’s year-end Hot Country Songs list. Big Loud/Apple Music No. 5: "Cowgirls" ft. Ernest Wallen enlisted the help of Ernest for this cowgirl anthem. The song is a celebration of the women who walk to the beat of their own drum — the ones that are wild and free, without any obligation for sticking around
“Cowgirls” arrived in April 2024 as the eighth single from his One Thing at a Time album. The song received country radio play and made its way up to the top spot on the Billboard Country Airplay chart. Big Loud No. 4: "You Proof" Playing off the idea of alcohol's proof, "You Proof" once again finds Wallen turning to booze to ease the pain of a breakup. When 90 and 100 proof aren't cutting it, he realizes he needs something "you proof."
"You Proof" was released a promotional single and is included on his 2023 album, One Thing at a Time . He wrote the song with Charlie Handsome, Ashley Gorley and Ernest. It debuted at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot Country Songs chart, replacing "Thought You Should Know" in that top spot. It's his fifth single to debut as a No. 1 on that chart. Although it's been bumped from No. 1 a few times, "You Proof" has spent 10 non-consecutive weeks on top, a new record in the chart's history. It's one of Morgan Wallen's best songs for a reason. Big Loud No. 3: "Thought You Should Know" Wallen lets his mama's boy flag fly in "Thought You Should Know." The track is a letter to his mother, telling her about all the things he has accomplished and assuring her that he is doing just fine. Wallen also promises his mama that her prayers about him have not gone unanswered.
He wrote the song with Miranda Lambert and Nicole Galyon as a tribute to his mom, Lesli. "Thought You Should Know" debuted at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot Country Songs chart, becoming his fourth single to do so. Coincidentally, he replaced his own song "Wasted on You" at the top spot making him the first artist to do that with a No. 1 debut. The song has been certified Platinum since. Republic/Apple Music No. 2: "I Had Some Help" with Post Malone It takes two to make a relationship, and it also takes two to break one. “I Had Some Help” speaks to that idea as both Wallen and Malone proclaim that they had help when it came to a relationship crashing and burning. The two remind their exes that they shouldn't throw stones in glass houses.
Wallen and Malone teamed up for the summer anthem in 2024. The song shot up the charts and topped several Billboard lists; Country Airplay, Hot 100, Hot Country Songs, Pop Airplay and Adult Pop Airplay. It also became a global sensation, landing in the Top 10 in several other countries. Terry Wyatt, Getty Images No. 1: "Last Night" Wallen sings about a night out with someone who knows he’s bad news. The two imbibed just a little too much and maybe went a little too far, at least in her eyes. And while she tries to swear him off completely, he sees in her eyes that she doesn’t really mean what she’s saying.
“Last Night” was a No. 1 hit for Wallen in 2023 on the country charts, but a career first chart-topper on the Billboard Hot 100 chart. Prior to that, the last time a solo male country artist landed at the peak of the list was Eddie Rabbitt in 1981 with “I Love a Rainy Night.” The song would then spend 16 non-consecutive weeks there, before earning a Grammy nomination at the 66th Grammy Awards. 3
